questiontext.text: What is the core definition of bullying in an educational environment?

answer.text: A single accidental bump into another student in a crowded corridor

feedback.text: Incorrect. Bullying is characterized by intentional aggression, an asymmetric balance of power, and repeated occurrences over time.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Bullying is characterized by intentional aggression, an asymmetric balance of power, and repeated occurrences over time.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Bullying is characterized by intentional aggression, an asymmetric balance of power, and repeated occurrences over time.

questiontext.text: Which of the following are recognized forms of non-physical bullying? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: Spreading rumors (relational), group boycotts (social exclusion), and cyberbullying are non-physical forms of bullying. Slapping and tripping are physical.

questiontext.text: Which of the following are common behavioral warning signs that a student may be experiencing bullying at school? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: Reluctance to attend school, unexplained injuries, damaged property, academic decline, and social withdrawal are classic warning signs of bullying.

questiontext.text: Match each category of bullying with its typical real-life example:

generalfeedback.text: Pushing and taking money is physical; derogatory names are verbal; excluding from games is relational; and online memes are cyberbullying.

questiontext.text: Match each role in school safety management with its core responsibility:

generalfeedback.text: The counselor provides psychological care; the duty teacher patrols during recess; the gatekeeper screens visitors; and the upstander student supports victims.
